title: The Chatbot Landscape
description: A clear map of the major AI chatbots — what each one is, who makes it, and when to use it.

data.text: There are now dozens of AI chatbots. But four dominate everyday use — ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini, and Perplexity. Each has genuine strengths and real limitations. This lesson gives you a honest, practical map of each one so you can pick the right tool for the right job.
The four you need to know

cards.title: ChatGPT (OpenAI)
cards.description: The most widely used AI chatbot in the world. Made by OpenAI. The flagship model is GPT-4o, which handles text, images, audio, and can interpret charts and screenshots. Has the richest plugin and API ecosystem.
cons: Context can degrade in very long chats

cards.title: Claude (Anthropic)
cards.description: Built by Anthropic, a safety-focused AI company. Known for nuanced, careful reasoning and handling very long documents. The 200K token context window is its standout feature — you can paste an entire book.
pros: Great at following complex multi-step instructions
cons: Can be overly cautious on edge-case requests

cards.title: Gemini (Google)
cards.description: Google's AI chatbot, deeply integrated into Google Workspace. If you live in Gmail, Docs, and Drive, Gemini blends into your environment in ways other chatbots cannot. Strong real-time web access and multimodal understanding.
cons: Responses can be longer and less precise
Best features need Google One AI Premium

cards.title: Perplexity
cards.description: An AI-powered search engine rather than a general chatbot. Every answer cites its sources. This dramatically reduces hallucination risk for factual questions. Think of it as Google + AI summary with footnotes.
pros: Every claim shows its source link
cons: Less useful for creative or coding tasks
Sources can still be wrong — verify important claims

rows: Editing or writing a long document
GPT-4o with some limits, no image generation
$20/month Google One AI Premium — Gemini Advanced

data.title: Start strategy
data.text: Start with one tool — ChatGPT or Claude — and use it for 2 weeks across different tasks. Then add Perplexity for research. Most power users eventually run 2-3 tools for different jobs, not one tool for everything.

data.title: Quick reference
points: ChatGPT — best overall, largest ecosystem, best free tier features
Claude — best for long documents, careful writing, complex instructions
Gemini — best with Google Workspace and for real-time web
Perplexity — best for factual research that needs cited sources
Most professionals use 2-3 tools — not one for everything
